title: CPR and cardiac arrest
description: A person is unresponsive and not breathing normally. Their heart may have stopped. Immediate chest compressions are needed.

recognition_questions.q: Is the person responsive when you shout and tap their shoulders?

immediate_safety_warnings: Check the scene is safe (traffic, fire, electricity, water) before touching the person.
If the person is on a bed, move them to a hard flat surface if you can do so safely.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Shout for help and ask someone to call 112 and find an AED if available.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Early emergency call and defibrillation save lives.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Tap the shoulders and shout 'Are you OK?'. If no response, the person is unresponsive.
Open the airway by tilting the head back and lifting the chin.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Opens the airway to check breathing.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Look, listen, and feel for normal breathing for up to 10 seconds. Agonal gasps are NOT normal breathing.
If not breathing normally, start chest compressions. Place the heel of one hand in the centre of the chest, other hand on top, push down 5-6 cm at 100-120 per minute.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Circulates blood to the brain and heart.

ordered_instructions.instruction: If trained and willing, give 2 rescue breaths after every 30 compressions. If not, do continuous compressions.
ordered_instructions.rationale: Provides oxygen; continuous compressions are acceptable if breaths are not possible.

ordered_instructions.instruction: Continue CPR until: the person starts breathing, an AED arrives and is ready, or emergency help takes over.
If an AED arrives, switch it on and follow its voice prompts.

actions_to_avoid: Do not delay CPR to feel for a pulse.
Do not stop CPR to check breathing more than once.
Do not give food or water.
Do not move the person unless they are in immediate danger.

escalation_conditions.condition: Person is unresponsive and not breathing normally
You are alone with no phone
escalation_conditions.action: Do 1 minute of CPR, then leave briefly to call 112, then resume
Place in recovery position, monitor, call 112 if not already called

approved_alternatives.alternative: One-handed compressions for a child if you cannot manage two hands
Continuous CPR until emergency services arrive if no AED is available

follow_up_requirements: All cardiac arrest survivors must be assessed in hospital.
Record the time CPR started and any AED shocks delivered.

age_specific_pathways.adult: Hand position: centre of chest. Depth: 5-6 cm. Ratio 30:2.
age_specific_pathways.child: Use one or two hands. Depth: 5 cm (1/3 chest depth). Ratio 30:2 (15:2 if two rescuers).
age_specific_pathways.infant: Use two fingers in the centre of the chest. Depth: 4 cm (1/3 chest depth). Ratio 30:2 (15:2 if two rescuers). Give gentle puffs for breaths, not full breaths.

source_references.document: International First Aid, Resuscitation and Education Guidelines
